QASHANI:81:10-17/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:81:10-17/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:81:10-17/r1.claim: Unfolded books are the faculties’ and souls’ pages containing deeds; they are folded at death when the spirit’s sun is rolled up, then opened at resurrection and return to the body.
QASHANI:81:10-17/r1.anchor: صحائف القوى والنفوس التي فيها هيئات الأعمال تطوى عند الموت

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p194/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p194/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p194/r2.claim: After resurrection, people are sorted by belief and deeds, the oppressed receive justice, records are exposed, the sky reddens, Hell blazes, Paradise nears, and each sees what he has prepared.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p194/r2.anchor: the circumstances which will arise after the dead are brought back to life are portrayed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p200/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p200/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p200/r1.claim: The opened scrolls are each person's record of deeds, with every deed brought into view, as confirmed by 81:14.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p200/r1.anchor: laying them open means that each and every deed will be brought before them

BIQAI-FULL:v8p335/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p335/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p335/r1.claim: Al-Takwīr threatens the Day of Judgment as the climactic display of divine majesty and warns those who reject the Qur’an, a reminder preserved in honored, pure pages by angelic scribes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p335/r1.anchor: مقصودها التهديد الشديد بيوم الوعيد الذي هو محط الرحال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p335#s081/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p335#s081/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p335#s081/r1.claim: Al-Takwīr threatens the climactic Day of Judgment and chastises Qur’an deniers; the Qur’an is a reminder in honored, pure pages delivered by trusted angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p335#s081/r1.anchor: مقصودها التهديد الشديد بيوم الوعيد الذي هو محط الرحال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r1.claim: The cosmic signs in al-Takwīr precede the flight from relatives in ʿAbasa, so the opening of this surah signals the Hour and answers when it will come.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r1.anchor: ووقوع تكوير الشمس وانكدار النجوم وتسيير الجبال وتعطيل العشار كل ذلك متقدم على فرار المرء من أخيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r2.claim: After associating disgrace with the verse about humanity’s ingratitude, Biqāʿī says the gravest denial after shirk is rejecting the truth, especially the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p340/r2.anchor: وأعظمه التكذيب بالقرآن , وذلك التكذيب هو الذي جمع الخزي

JISHUMI:v10p7301/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7301/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7301/r6.anchor: ومنها: أن الأعمال مكتوبة في الصحف

ELMALILI:81:1-16#2/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#2/r30.speaker: Ebû Âliye
ELMALILI:81:1-16#2/r30.claim: Abū ʿĀliya divides the surah into six signs witnessed in this world, from the sun through the seas, and six belonging to the afterlife, from the souls being paired through Paradise being brought near.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#2/r30.anchor: Abd b. Humeyd ve İbn Münzir Ebû Âliye’den rivayet etmişlerdir ki bu sûreden altı âyet dünyada ve insanlar bakarlarken, altısı da âhirettedir.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#6/r3.claim: The repeated conditional clauses each alert the reader to an independently awesome event; although a single opening conditional might suffice, the answer is attached to them collectively.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#6/r3.anchor: her birinin müstakillen dehşet ve ehemmiyetine tenbih için اِذَا’lar tekrar edilmiş ve hüküm, mecmû‘una rabtolunmuştur.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r1.speaker: قوم
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports a group's allegorical reading of the signs as metaphors for each human and the circumstances of death, including the sun as the self and stars as senses.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r1.anchor: İbn Atıyye tefsirinde demiştir ki: “Bir kavim bu zikrolunan şeylerin benî Âdem’den her biri ve ölüm sırasındaki ahvâl hakkında istiareler

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r2.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan calls this symbolic reading a doctrine of Batiniyya and extreme Sufis who attach themselves to Islam under cover while secretly rejecting it.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r2.anchor: Ebû Hayyân da bunu naklettikten sonra şöyle demiştir: “Bu Bâtıniyye mezhebi ve gulât-ı sûfiyyeden İslâm’a müntesib olanların mezhebleridir.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r3.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan says the Qur'an is clear Arabic and contains no symbols, riddles, inner meanings, or allusions to philosophical and naturalist teachings.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r3.anchor: Kitâbullah بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّۢ مُّبِينٍۢ [eş-Şu‘arâ 26/195] gelmiştir. Onda ne remiz ne lügaz ne bâtın yoktur.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r4.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan criticizes Fakhr al-Din al-Razi for inserting philosophers', astrologers', and astronomers' opinions into his commentary as far from Qur'anic exegesis.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r4.anchor: İbn Hatîb-i Rey nâmıyla mâruf Ebû Abdullâh Râzî

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r5.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan likewise objects to Sufi statements called 'truths' in Tahrir and Tahbir, some of which he says should not even be written.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r5.anchor: sâhibinin tefsir ettiği âyetlerin âhirinde sûfiyye müntesiblerinin kelâmlarından zikrettiği

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r6.claim: The author says Abu Hayyan's polemic is excessive and deficient in balance.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r6.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Ebû Hayyân’ın bu sözleri ifrat ve tefritten hâlî değildir.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r7.claim: The Qur'an was revealed in clear Arabic, and its language is not itself an obscure symbolic code.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r7.anchor: Şüphe yok ki Kelâmullah lisân-ı Arabî-i mübîn

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r8.claim: A text should ordinarily be taken in its apparent sense unless a contextual indication prevents that reading.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r8.anchor: nusûsta aslolan bir karîne-i mâni‘a bulunmadıkça zâhiri üzere hamlolunmaktır.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r9.claim: Alongside clear passages, the Qur'an has hidden, difficult, concise, and ambiguous passages and uses literal, figurative, explicit, implicit, allegorical, and rhetorical forms.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r9.anchor: Kur’ân’ın ümmü’l-kitâb olan muhkemâtının yanında hafî, müşkil, mücmel ve müteşâbihâtı, hakikati, mecazı, sarîhi, kinâyesi, istiâresi

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r10.claim: The clearest sense remains intended, while further secondary implications may also be sought alongside it.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r10.anchor: Bütün bunlarda en vâzıh olan mâna maksud olmakla beraber “müstetbe‘ât-i terâkîb” denilen ve derece-i tâliyede matlub olan nice ifadeler de vardır.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r11.claim: Such secondary implications cannot contradict the clear explanation of decisive passages and are compatible with clear Arabic expression.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r11.anchor: zâhire münâfî ve münâkız olmayarak maiyyetinde bazı ihtimâlât ile derece-i tâliyede

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r12.claim: It is wrong to claim the Qur'an contains no inner sense, symbol, or indication; the disconnected opening letters remain symbolic regardless of their interpretation.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r12.anchor: الٓمٓ، قٓ، نٓ gibi mukatta‘ât-ı süver ne suretle tefsir edilirse edilsin remzî olmaktan hâlî denemez.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r13.speaker: آثار
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r13.claim: Some transmitted reports say the Qur'an has an outward and inward meaning, as well as a limit and a point of ascent.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r13.anchor: Doğrusu bazı âsârda dahi vârid olduğu üzere Kur’ân’ın hem zâhiri vardır hem bâtını, hem haddi vardır hem matla‘ı.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r14.claim: Outward and inward meanings cannot conflict, since the Qur'an is free of disagreement and contradiction, as 4:82 states.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r14.anchor: hakikatte ihtilâf ve tenakuzdan âzâde eblağ bir kitâb-ı mübîn olduğu için zâhiri ile bâtını arasında tehâlüf ve tebâyünden de münezzehtir.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r15.claim: The meeting of outward and inward meanings resembles two seas meeting behind a boundary that prevents either from transgressing, as in 55:19–20.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r15.anchor: birbirine bağy u tecavüzüne mâni‘olan haddi aşılmamak şartıyla

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r16.claim: Spiritually inspired insights within those bounds have no end, just as the Lord's words exceed the sea's ink, as in 18:109.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r16.anchor: ondan zaman zaman vehbî ve zevkī olarak alınan tulû‘ât ve ilhâmâta bir nihâyet de tasavvur olunamaz.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r17.claim: It is wrong to deny that the Qur'an has indications about human ideas and concerns, or to censure interpreters such as Razi for illuminating them.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r17.anchor: Râzî gibi o yolda tenvîr-i efkâra hizmet edenlere ta‘n etmek doğru olmadığı gibi

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r18.claim: Sufi commentaries that discuss spiritual insights without nullifying the text's clear sense and rulings should not all be classed with heretical esotericists.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r18.anchor: sûfiyye tefsirlerinin hepsini de Karâmita ve Hurûfiyye bâtıniyyesi gibi zenâdıkadan saymak da doğru değildir.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r19.claim: Kashani and Ara'is should not be treated like Hasan Sabbah's and extreme Imamite books that nullify the Qur'an's outward meanings and rulings.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r19.anchor: mahza zâhirî olan me‘ânî ve ahkâmı ibtal vadisinde yazılmış Hasan Sabbah

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r20.claim: Abandoning decisive passages to pursue ambiguous ones for discord and distortive interpretation arises from a crooked heart, as 3:7 warns.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r20.anchor: kalb çarpıklığından, rûh bozukluğundan neş’et eden bir zeyğ u ilhaddır.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r21.claim: Ignoring the insights of interpreters who first establish outward meanings and rulings, then offer compatible indications, would be a loss.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r21.anchor: sânihâtından istifade etmemek de mahrumiyet olur.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r22.claim: The Qur'an addresses people according to their qualities and capacities, speaking to believers, thinkers, knowers, rememberers, the pious, and people of understanding at different levels.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r22.anchor: muhatabların evsâf ve kābiliyet-i mahsûsalarıyla derecelerine göre türlü mazmunlarla hitap edip dururken

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r23.claim: Commentary's attention to intellectual and moral levels serves the Qur'an's aims of illumination and its levels of meaning.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r23.anchor: Kur’ân’ın hadd ü matla‘ına ve umûmu tenvîre mâtuf olan makāsıdına uygun da olmaz.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r24.claim: Excessive literalism is as harmful as excessive esotericism; the author invokes those learned in knowledge acting justly, as in 3:18.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r24.anchor: Her hâlde zâhirîlikte ifrat etmek de bâtınîlikte ifrat etmek kadar muzırdır.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r25.claim: The Qur'an includes both tafsir and ta'wil.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r25.anchor: Ve Kur’an’da tefsir de vardır, tevil de vardır.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r30.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r30.claim: Considering possible metaphors in events whose details remain unknown is neither illegitimate symbolism nor esoteric deviation; it helps make the great resurrection imaginable through the lesser events and strengthen faith.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r30.anchor: Bilakis kıyâmet-i kübrâ vukū‘âtını kıyâmet-i suğrâ vukū‘âtıyla ezhâna takrib ederek imanı takviyeye çalışmaktır.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r31.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r31.speaker: Nizâmüddîn Nîsâbûrî
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r31.claim: Nisaburi first interprets these verses according to their apparent sense, then records the interpreters' reflections on the lesser resurrection.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r31.anchor: Nizâmüddîn Nîsâbûrî Garâibu’l-Kur’ân ve Regāibu’l-Furkān nâm tefsirinde bu âyetleri zâhiri vechile usul dairesinde tefsir ettikten sonra ehl-i tevilin zikri geçen kavillerini de şöyle kaydetmiştir:

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r32.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r32.speaker: أهل التأويل
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r32.claim: The interpreters apply these events to the lesser resurrection, the state of death.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r32.anchor: Ehl-i tevil dediler ki bu ahvâli kıyâmet-i suğrâ hakkında da itibar etmek mümkindir. Kıyâmet-i suğrâ ise mevt hâlidir.

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r43.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r43.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r43.claim: The interpreters' readings do not deny the great resurrection; they also draw lessons about the certain lesser resurrection of death, which benefits faith and creed.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r43.anchor: muradları bu âyetlerin esas itibariyle kıyâmet-i kübrâ hakkında olduğunu nefy ü inkâr değil

ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r45.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r45.speaker: author
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r45.claim: All these reflections culminate in the great resurrection, the verses' true subject, when reality is fully unveiled and every soul knows its deeds at final judgment.
ELMALILI:81:1-16#7/r45.anchor: hepsinin tamamı kıyâmet-i kübrâdadır. Ve bu âyetler, asıl onun hakkındadır. Bütün hakk u hakikatin inkişâfı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r30.claim: Deeds registers are closed when people die to be opened on the Day of Judgment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r30.anchor: İnsanlar öldüklerinde hesap gününde açılmak üzere amel defterleri kapanır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r31.claim: When the registers are displayed, everyone sees and recalls all the good and evil they did, and judgment is then carried out according to those deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:81:1/r31.anchor: herkes, dünyada iken hayır veya şer adına ne işlemişse kendi amel defterinde yazılmış olduğunu görür ve yaptıklarını hatırlar. Hesabı görüldükten sonra artık hakkında amellerine göre işlem yapılır

DURR-FULL:v8p427/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p427/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p427/r7.claim: Qatāda says each person's record is dictated, folded, then spread open on the Day of Resurrection for its owner to see what it contains.
DURR-FULL:v8p427/r7.anchor: صحيفتك يا ابن آدم يملي ما فيها ثم تطوى ثم تنشر عليك يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p441#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p441#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p441#2/r1.claim: The listed events are all descriptions of the Day of Resurrection.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r3.claim: The spread-out pages are interpreted either as records opened for everyone to read or as pages flying to right and left according to recompense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r3.anchor: و «الصحف المنشورة» : قيل هي صحف الأعمال تنشر ليقرأ كل امرئ كتابه، وقيل هي الصحف التي تتطاير بالأيمان، والشمائل بالجزاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r4.speaker: نافع، ابن عامر، عاصم، أبو جعفر، شيبة، الأعرج، الحسن، أبو رجاء، قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r4.claim: These readers pronounce nushirat with a light shīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وأبو جعفر وشيبة والأعرج والحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة: «نشرت» بتخفيف الشين المكسورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r5.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r5.claim: These readers geminate the shīn for emphasis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p442#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي: «نشرت» بشد الشين على المبالغة

JISHUMI:v10p7295/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read نشرت with doubling, and سجرت and سعرت without doubling.
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو نشرت بالتشديد، وسجرت وسعرت بالتخفيف

JISHUMI:v10p7295/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r8.claim: Abu Amr, Nafiʿ, Ibn Amir, and Asim read نشرت without doubling, but double سجرت and سعرت.
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع، وابن عامر، وعاصم: نشرت مخففة سجرت وسعرت مشددتين

JISHUMI:v10p7295/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r9.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r9.claim: Abu Bakr transmits from Asim a doubled سجرت and undoubled نشرت and سعرت.
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r9.anchor: وروى أبو بكر عن عاصم سجرت مشددة، ونشرت وسعرت مخففتين؟

JISHUMI:v10p7295/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r10.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r10.claim: A similar reading is transmitted from Yaqub, who is also said to read all three forms without doubling.
JISHUMI:v10p7295/r10.anchor: وروي نحوه عن يعقوب، وقرأ يعقوب كله خفيفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r7.claim: Nushirat has light and doubled readings; the records are folded when a person dies and then spread at the accounting.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r7.anchor: ( نشرت ) قرىء بالتخفيف والتشديد ، يريد : صحف الأعمال تطوى صحيفة الإنسان عند موته ، ثم تنتشر إذا حوسب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r8.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r8.claim: Qatāda says each person’s page is folded over his deeds and then opened on the Resurrection Day, so everyone should watch what he writes in it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r8.anchor: عن قتادة : صحيفتك يا ابن آدم تطوى على عملك ، ثم تنشر يوم القيامة ، فلينظر رجل ما يملي في صحيفته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r9.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r9.claim: When ʿUmar recited the verse, he would say that the matter is being carried to God, son of Adam.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r9.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه كان إذا قرأها قال : إليك يساق الأمر يا ابن آدم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r10.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r10.claim: The Prophet says people will be resurrected barefoot and naked; when Umm Salamah asks about women, he replies that people are too occupied, and explains that the spread records contain even minute measures of dust and mustard seed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r10.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r11.speaker: مرثد بن وداعة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r11.claim: Marṯad ibn Wadāʿah says records fly from beneath the Throne: the believer receives a page in a high garden, while the disbeliever receives one in scorching wind and hot water, meaning that this is what the page records.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p708/r11.anchor: وعن مرثد بن وداعة : إذا كان يوم القيامة تطايرت الصحف من تحت العرش ، فتقع صحيفة المؤمن في يده في جنة عالية ، وتقع صحيفة الكافر في يده في سموم وحميم

MUQATIL:81:1-7/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:81:1-7/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:81:1-7/r11.claim: A person's record is folded at death and opened for jinn and humans on Resurrection.
MUQATIL:81:1-7/r11.anchor: وذلك أن المرء إذا مات طويت صحيفته، فإذا كان يوم القيامة نشرت للجن والإنس فيعطون كتبهم،

MUQATIL:81:1-7/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:81:1-7/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:81:1-7/r12.claim: The guardian angels give each person an opened book in the right or left hand.

RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r8.claim: كشطت means uncovered and removed from what lies above it, Paradise and God's Throne, like stripping skin from a slaughtered animal or removing a cover.
RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r8.anchor: أي كشفت وأزيلت عما فوقها ، وهو الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r9.claim: Ibn Masud reads قشطت; al-Farra says it means stripped away and then folded, and the k/q alternation is common.
RAZI-FULL:v31p64/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : قشطت ، واعتقاب القاف والكاف كثير ، يقال لبكت الثريد ولبقته ، والكافور والقافور ، قال الفراء : نزعت فطويت

THALABI:v10p139/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p139/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p139/r7.claim: The reciters of Medina, Syria, and Basra except Abu Amr read nushirat lightly; other readers used the doubled consonant, supported by the phrase in 74:52.
THALABI:v10p139/r7.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام والبصرة إلا أبا عمرو بالتخفيف غيرهم بالتشديد لقوله سبحانه صحفا منشرة

THALABI:v10p139/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p139/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p139/r8.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet said people will be resurrected naked and barefoot.
THALABI:v10p139/r8.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «يحشر الناس يوم القيامة عراة حفاة»

THALABI:v10p139/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p139/r9.speaker: أم سلمة
THALABI:v10p139/r9.claim: Umm Salama reports asking about women and being told by the Prophet that people are occupied because the records spread with dust- and mustard-seed weights.
THALABI:v10p139/r9.anchor: قال: «شغل الناس يا أم سلمة» قالت: وما شغلهم قال: «نشر الصحف فيها مثاقيل الذر ومثاقيل الخردل»

NAHHAS:v5p157/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p157/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر، شيبة، نافع؛ أبو عمرو، ابن كثير، يحيى، الأعمش، حمزة، الكسائي
NAHHAS:v5p157/r11.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, and Nafi read one vocalization of nushirat; Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, and al-Kisai read the other.
NAHHAS:v5p157/r11.anchor: لأن نشرت يقع للقليل والكثير عند النحويين والقراءتان صحيحتان

NAHHAS:v5p157/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p157/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p157/r12.claim: The “opened scrolls” parallel in 74:52 does not compel abandoning the other reading: both readings are sound, and grammarians allow nushirat for few or many.
NAHHAS:v5p157/r12.anchor: والحجة لهم ﴿ صحفا منشرة ﴾ وهذا ليس من الحجج الموجبة لترك ما قرأ به من تقوم بقراءته الحجة

SAMIN-DURR:81:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:81:10/r1.speaker: الأخوان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:81:10/r1.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr read نشرت with gemination; the others read it without gemination.
SAMIN-DURR:81:10/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالتثقيل. والباقون بالتخفيف.

ZAJJAJ:v5p290/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p290/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p290/r1.claim: The records are opened and each person receives a book in the right or left hand according to their deeds.
ZAJJAJ:v5p290/r1.anchor: ونشرت. نشرت الصحف وأعطى كل إنسان كتابه بيمينه أو بشماله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r1.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r1.claim: Al-Jurjani's al-Risala al-Shafiya develops his argument for Qur'anic inimitability; he considers it persuasive to someone with receptive taste, but not to one lacking the faculty to understand it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r1.anchor: ومع الدلائل، قدم الجرجاني (الرسالة الشافية) فى إعجاز القرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r2.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r2.claim: Al-Jurjani compares understanding this rhetorical field to judging poetry: without the requisite taste, someone may wrongly assume they possess the needed competence and issue uninformed judgments.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r2.anchor: وكما لا يقيم الشعر فى نفس من لا ذوق له، لا يفهم هذا البابَ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r3.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r3.claim: He says argument works only with a listener willing to attend and follow its direction; then resistance can turn into ease and acceptance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r3.anchor: حتى تجد مَن فيه عون لك، ومن إذا أبى عليك أي ذاك طبعُه فردَّه إليك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r4.speaker: ابن حزم الظاهري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r4.claim: Bint al-Shatiʾ notes that Ibn Hazm, in the fifth century, challenged earlier writers on inimitability and sharply criticized al-Baqillani.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p25/r4.anchor: فى القرن الخامس أيضاً، ظهر ابن حزم الظاهرى (ت 456 هـ) فتصدى للسلف ممن تكلموا فى إعجاز القرآن

QIRAAT-ER:81:10:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:81:10:4#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:81:10:4#1/r1.claim: The Vr Form II passive with shadda intensifies or distributes the action, making the records spread thoroughly, repeatedly, or one after another.
QIRAAT-ER:81:10:4#1/r1.anchor: Canonical Form II passive with shadda intensifies or distributes the action: the records are made to be spread thoroughly

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r3.claim: The records of deeds, previously folded, are spread on the Day of Resurrection so each person can read their book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r3.anchor: صحف الأعمال كانت مطوية على الأعمال، فنشرت يوم القيامة ليقرأ كل إنسان كتابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r4.claim: Another view identifies the pages as records flying to people on their right and left with their recompense, distinct from the deeds scrolls.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r4.anchor: وقيل: الصحف التي تتطاير بالأيمان والشمائل بالجزاء، وهي صحف غير صحف الأعمال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء وقتادة والحسن والأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r5.claim: These readers pronounce the shin lightly; the rest of the Seven pronounce it geminated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p417/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء وقتادة والحسن والأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم: نشرت بخف الشين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r1.claim: The scrolls are records of deeds; Ibn Jurayj says a person's record is folded at death, then opened on resurrection for judgment according to its contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج أنه قال إذا مات الإنسان طويت صحيفته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r2.speaker: مرثد بن وداعة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r2.claim: Mirthad ibn Wadaʿa says the pages are distributed among their owners: on Judgment Day they fly from beneath the Throne, the believer's page falling into his hand in a high garden and the unbeliever's in scorching wind and boiling water; these are not deeds records.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r2.anchor: عن مرثد بن وداعة إذا كان يوم القيامة تطايرت الصحف من تحت العرش

ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza, and al-Kisai read nushshirat with a doubled shīn, conveying intensified spreading, many pages, or especially forceful flight.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p55/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي نشرت بالتشديد للمبالغة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r6.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام وعاصم ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r6.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb read nushirat lightly; the remaining readers double it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r6.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام وعاصم ويعقوب: "نشرت" بالتخفيف، وقرأ الآخرون بالتشديد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r7.claim: The spread pages are records of deeds opened for reckoning, as in the phrase about pages spread out in al-Muddaththir.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p348/r7.anchor: كقوله: "يؤتى صحفا منشرة" (المدثر-52) يعني صحائف الأعمال تنتشر للحساب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r1.claim: The sheets are records of deeds, folded at death and spread out at the reckoning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r1.anchor: يعني صحف الأعمال فإنها تطوى عند الموت وتنشر وقت الحساب

BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r2.claim: Alternatively, the sheets are distributed among their recipients.

BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read with a doubled shīn for emphasis, numerous sheets, or intense dispersal.
BAYDAWI-FULL:81:10-14/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي بالتشديد للمبالغة في النشر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r1.claim: The universal questioning leads to signs of the ensuing bliss or punishment, beginning with the opening of the records.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r1.anchor: ولما دل هذا على عموم السؤال , ذكر ما ينشأ عنه مما يدل على النعيم أو النكال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r2.claim: The scrolls are the sheets on which people’s deeds have been written.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r2.anchor: أي الأوراق التي كتبت فيها أعمال العباد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r3.claim: The records are unfolded widely before their owners with ease: the blessed receive theirs in the right hand from before, while the wretched receive theirs behind the back and in the left after they were folded at death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r3.anchor: فتأتي السعيد في يمينه من تلقاء وجهه على وجه يكون فيه بشارة له , وتأتي الشقي من وراء ظهره وفي شماله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r4.claim: Because the record will either save or ruin its owner, a person who believes in it should put only good words, deeds, and beliefs into it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p338/r4.anchor: فمن اعتقد أن صحيفته ثابتة فترديه أو تنجيه لم يضع فيها إلا حسنا من قول أو عمل أو اعتقاد

DURR-FULL:v8p431/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p431/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p431/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says a person’s record is folded when the person dies, then opened on the Day of Resurrection for judgment according to its contents.
DURR-FULL:v8p431/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج {وإذا الصحف نشرت} قال: إذا مات الإنسان طويت صحيفته ثم تنشر يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r5.claim: Nashr literally means opening a scroll's folds or unwrapping it so its writing can be read; compare the spread scrolls in 74:52 and the open book in 17:13.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r5.anchor: ونشر الصحف حقيقته : فتح طيات الصحيفة ، أو إطلاق التفافها لتقرأ كتابتها ، وتقدم في قوله : { أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r6.claim: The scrolls are records of deeds, either actual pages unlike familiar ones or a metaphor for things that enumerate people's deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r6.anchor: والمراد : صحف الأعمال ، وهي إما صحف حقيقية مخالفة للصحف المألوفة ، وإما مجازية أطلقت على أشياء فيها إحصاء أعمال الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqūb read with a light shīn; the majority geminate it to suggest the many scrolls being spread.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p148/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وأبو جعفر ويعقوب : { نشرت } بتخفيف الشين . وقرأه الجمهور بتشديد الشين للتكثير لكثرة الصحف المنشورة .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو جعفر وابن عامر ويعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r1.claim: Nafi, Asim, Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub read nushirat with a light consonant; the remaining readers double it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وعاصم وأبو جعفر وابن عامر ويعقوب نشرت بالتخفيف والباقون بالتشديد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r2.claim: The scrolls are the records of the deeds of Adam’s descendants, spread out for the reckoning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p40#3/r2.anchor: والمراد بالصحف صحائف أعمال بني آدم تنشر للحساب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says each person receives his record in the right or left hand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r3.anchor: قال الضحاك: أعطي كل إنسان صحيفته بيمينه أو بشماله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r4.claim: Qatada says each person’s record is written, folded, and spread on Judgment Day, so one should watch what one writes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p335/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: [صحيفتك] (6) يا ابن آدم، تملى فيها،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r9.claim: The scrolls are records of deeds in which the angels wrote each person's good and evil actions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r9.anchor: يعني صحف الأعمال إذا كتب الملائكة فيها ما فعل أهلها من خير وشر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r10.claim: The records are folded at death and unfolded at the resurrection, when each person sees and learns the contents of their own record.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r10.anchor: وتنشر في القيامة ، فيقف كل إنسان على صحيفته

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r11.claim: Al-Māwardī supports the account of each person confronting their record with Qur'an 18:49.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r11.anchor: ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r12.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read نشرت with a doubled shadda, indicating repeated unfolding.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بتشديد نشرت على تكرار النشر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r13.speaker: الباقون
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r13.claim: The other readers use the light form, indicating that the records are unfolded once.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r13.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتخفيف على نشرها مرة واحدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r14.claim: If the unfolding is once, its purpose is to establish the proof against people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r14.anchor: فإن حمل على المرة الواحدة فلقيام الحجة بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r15.claim: If unfolding is repeated, one explanation is to intensify the rebuke of sinners and the glad tidings given to the obedient.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r15.anchor: للمبالغة في تقريع العاصي وتبشير المطيع

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r16.claim: A second explanation for repeated unfolding is that the person and the angel witnesses repeatedly review the record.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p214/r16.anchor: لتكرير ذلك من الإنسان والملائكة الشهداء عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r1.speaker: مدنى وشامى وعاصم وسهل ويعقوب
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r1.claim: Madinan, Syrian, ʿĀṣim, Sahl, and Yaʿqūb read nushirat with lightening (takhfīf).
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r1.anchor: فتحت بالتخفيف مدنى وشامى وعاصم وسهل ويعقوب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r2.claim: The scrolls are records of deeds, folded at a person's death and opened when that person is judged.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r2.anchor: والمراد صحف الأعمال تطوى صحيفة الانسان عند موته ثم تنشر إذا حوسب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r3.claim: Alternatively, the scrolls are distributed among their owners.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p319#10/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد نشرت بين أصحابها أى فرقت بينهم

QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r12.claim: نشرت means opened after having been folded.
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r12.anchor: أي فتحت بعد أن كانت مطوية

QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r13.claim: The sheets are records of deeds in which angels wrote their owners' good and evil; they are folded at death and spread on Resurrection Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r13.anchor: والمراد صحف الأعمال التي كتبت الملائكة فيها ما فعل أهلها من خير وشر، تطوى بالموت، وتنشر في يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r14.claim: Each person sees and knows the contents of their own record, as illustrated by 18:49.
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r14.anchor: فيقف كل إنسان على صحيفته، فيعلم ما فيها، فيقول: ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها [الكهف: 49]

QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r15.speaker: مرثد بن وداعة
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r15.claim: Marthad ibn Wada'a reports that on Judgment Day the records fly from beneath the Throne, and the believer's record lands in his hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:81:10/r15.anchor: وروى مرثد بن وداعة قال: إذا كان يوم القيامة تطايرت الصحف من تحت العرش، فتقع صحيفة المؤمن في يده

STUDYQURAN:81:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:81:10/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:81:10/r1.claim: The spread pages are the opening of the record of deeds; at Judgment people review an exhaustive account, as in 18:49, and no deed is hidden. Related passages describe the record books and their contents.
STUDYQURAN:81:10/r1.anchor: When the pages are spread refers to the opening of the book in which people’s deeds are recorded.

TAB-FULL:v24p149/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r1.claim: The servants' records, containing good and bad deeds, are opened after having been folded.
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r1.anchor: صحيفتك يا ابن آدم، تملي ما فيها

TAB-FULL:v24p149/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r2.claim: Qatāda says each person's record is filled with its contents, folded, then opened to that person on Resurrection Day.

TAB-FULL:v24p149/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r3.speaker: قراء المدينة وبعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r3.claim: Most Medinan readers and some Kufans read nushirat with a light shīn.

TAB-FULL:v24p149/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r4.speaker: بعض قراء مكة وعامة قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r4.claim: Some Meccan readers and most Kufans read nushshirat with a doubled shīn.
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r4.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض قراء مكة وعامة قراء الكوفة بتشديد الشين

TAB-FULL:v24p149/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r5.claim: The doubled reading is supported by 74:52's munashshara rather than manshūra; doubling suits the plural, like “slaughtered camels,” while a singular would be light.
TAB-FULL:v24p149/r5.anchor: بقول الله: {أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة} [المدثر: 52] ولم يقل منشورة

TABATABAI:81:10-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:81:10-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:81:10-14/r2.claim: The scrolls are the records of deeds, opened for reckoning.

FARRA:v3p240/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p240/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p240/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab and his companions double the verb; other Medinans and readers lighten it. Both work: 74:52 has منشرة, while منشورة is ordinary Arabic; plural usage permits both forms, unlike the singular رجل مقتول.
FARRA:v3p240/r3.anchor: شددها يحيى بن وثاب، وأصحابه، وخففها آخرون من أهل المدينة وغيرهم. وكل صواب، قال الله جل وعز «صحفا منشرة » ، فهذا شاهد لمن شدد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r1.claim: The pages are the records of the children of Adam, which are spread open.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r2.claim: Muqatil says a person's record is folded at death, then opened on Judgment Day and handed to him open by the record-keeping angels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: إن المرء إذا مات طويت صحيفة (¬2) أعماله، فإذا كان يوم القيامة نشرت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r3.claim: The commentators likewise explain that the records are spread open for reckoning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p261/r3.anchor: ونحو هذا قال المفسرون (¬4): نشرت للحساب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:81:9-15/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:81:9-15/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:81:9-15/r3.claim: The scrolls are the books of deeds.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r1.claim: The classification of detailed similes follows common patterns; their finest distinctions cannot be fully bounded.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r1.anchor: هذه القسمة في التفصيل موضوعة على الأغلب الأعرف وإلا فدقائقه لا تكاد تضبط

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r2.claim: One compound-simile type requires a whole set of features in a particular arrangement, as in narcissus like pearl bowls containing agate.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون شيئا بقدر المشبه وبصفته أولا يكون ومثال ذلك تشبيه النرجس بمداهن در حشوهن عقيق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r3.claim: In this type, removing a component or changing how the components meet destroys the intended likeness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r3.anchor: فقد حصله في النرجس من شكل المداهن والعقيق بشرط أن تكون المداهن من الدر وأن يكون العقيق في الحشو منها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r4.claim: The other type compares a configuration formed by two paired things, not each thing separately; dawn beneath night is likened to a gray horse beneath a covering.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r4.anchor: قصد الشبه الحاصل لك إذا نظرت إلى الصبح والليل جميعا وتأملت حالهما معا وأراد أن يأتي بنظير للهيئة المشاهدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r5.claim: The paired configuration in the second type is an observed, familiar possibility rather than a relation that exists only in imagination.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p146/r5.anchor: ثم إن هذا الاقتران الذي وضع عليه التشبيه مما يوجد ويعهد إذ ليس وجود الفرس الأشهب قد ألقى الجل

NASHR:v2p398/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p398/r3.speaker: المدنيان وابن عامر ويعقوب وعاصم
NASHR:v2p398/r3.claim: The two Medinans, Ibn Amir, Yaqub, and Asim read nushirat with a light shin; the remaining readers double it.
NASHR:v2p398/r3.anchor: نشرت فقرأ المدنيان، وابن عامر، ويعقوب، وعاصم بتخفيف الشين، وقرأ الباقون بتشديدها
